chapter: Harlem, 52nd Street and the first big bands
title: Personnel of the Paramount band and Hammond's Melody Maker praise
summary: Barnet names the sidemen, led by arranger Nathan Van Cleve, and recalls Hammond's review of the special arrangements and the musicians' ball.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Do you remember who was in that band, that first band?

Yeah. Well, the guy that was making all the arrangements was Nathan Van Cleve, who later became quite a big heavy in the studios here, out in the West Coast, arranging. He was playing trumpet in the band. Johnny Dillard, Bob Kuzamano, and Doug Shoffner. That was the trumpet section. And the trombone player was Wally Baron. Let's see, Billy Speer was the baritone saxophone player, and Stu -- Stu, Stu, Stu, come on Stu, where are you -- Stu something was the tenor, and -- I've got a couple of blank faces there. Bill Long and Horace Diaz were the piano players. Bill King was the bass player. And Scoop Thompson was the guitar player.
I remembered more of those than I thought I was going to.
Yeah. So what was John Hammond's reaction to the band?

Oh, he wrote about our band, because we were playing all special arrangements, see, and this was unheard of around New York, except possibly the Goldkette band, when they would come in, or something like that, and he enthused in The Melody Maker about the band, and I remember we went over the play the musicians' ball, which was a command performance, you know, and we completely broke the place up. The musicians were screaming and hollering and of course that is the greatest accolade you can get in the world. It's nice from people, but when it comes from you know, your own group, it really means something.
